limits: Full goal, 0B, 2A, U4/U6/U7 and implementation/release gates remain open. These results establish the listed behaviors, not full support.

Reference encoding is currently used by setDoc and where. The path-only legacy marker still needs qualified project/database identity, collision handling, validation, other write factories and operations, cursors, and events/capture propagation. The encoder does not yet establish complete JSON-safe scalar encoding.

Stored reference values preserve their type and query identity. Browser snapshots bind usable references to the receiving port; host query decoding binds them to the query database. This does not establish full in-page nested-reference SDK behavior.
The two new SharedWorker scenarios are characterization, not claimed pre-implementation red cycles.
Earlier live-emulator and broader state/CLI evidence remains historical; the live browser leaf is unchanged in measured size. No live backend was contacted for this slice.
The additional S3 BridgeMount API seam remains pending; no tests at that interface have been authored.
Source identity covers changed files; a full transitive-input and completion verifier remains unfinished. CI commands were verified locally; no remote GitHub Actions run is claimed.
Hosted authority/persistence, complete observation delivery and Studio, reconnect/lifecycle, live operation surfaces and credential/release proofs remain required.

limits: Full goal, 0B, 2A, U4/U6/U7 and implementation/release gates remain open. These results establish the listed behaviors, not full support.

Current client modular write APIs and buffers encode registered references. Seven new S1 tests establish addDoc results and input, updateDoc, batch set/update, and transaction set/update; corresponding SharedWorker cases began green and are characterization.

The path-only legacy marker still requires qualified project/database identity, marker collision and invalid-value handling, remaining overloads and cursors, in-page nested-reference execution, and event/capture propagation. Complete JSON-safe scalar encoding remains unfinished.
The separate review-stage loop changes preserve five conflict attempts and named decisions; focused client/integration regressions and the final baseline pass.
Earlier live-emulator and broader state/CLI evidence remains historical. No live backend was contacted or remote CI run claimed for this slice.
The additional S3 BridgeMount API seam remains pending; no tests at that interface have been authored.

Source identity covers changed files; a full transitive-input and completion verifier remains unfinished. Hosted authority/persistence, observation/Studio, reconnect/lifecycle, live surfaces and credential/release proofs remain required.

limits: Full goal, 0B, 2A, U4/U6/U7 and implementation/release gates remain open. The listed behaviors do not establish complete runtime support.

Two timestamp and four reference-cursor S1 cycles have relevant red and green evidence. The existing Timestamp class moved unchanged into a browser-safe leaf; SDK decoding uses it while unary persistence decoding retains rules wrappers.

The SharedWorker timestamp cursor and hosted reference cursor started green and are characterization. All four value cursor forms now encode their operands, but snapshot overloads, converters, qualified identity, remaining scalar/marker/invalid-value behavior, and event/capture propagation remain required.

Studio imports the worker client, so its site assets were rebuilt and re-embedded before the final browser runs. Earlier browser runs from this slice used retained site assets and are superseded by the refreshed runs.
Earlier live-emulator and broader state/CLI evidence remains historical. No live backend was contacted or remote CI run claimed for this slice.
The additional S3 BridgeMount API seam remains pending; no tests at that interface have been authored.

Source identity covers changed files; a full transitive-input and completion verifier remains unfinished. Hosted authority/persistence, observation/Studio, reconnect/lifecycle, live surfaces and credential/release proofs remain required.

limits: Full goal, 0B, 2A/2D, U4/U6/U7 and implementation/release gates remain open. The listed cases do not establish complete runtime support.

Two S1 byte-value cycles establish the missing served Bytes export, SDK Bytes decoding and explicit bytes encoding before SharedWorker cloning. The original named-import diagnostic never reached the operation and is not substituted for the later relevant red assertion.

The existing Bytes class moved to a browser-safe leaf and retained its original export. Separate review uses Uint8Array.from for Latin-1 base64 input and named JSON decisions with a readonly unknown-property view, preserving marker-first short-circuiting and property access order. Existing rules bytes and the unary persistence decoder retain their representation.

Eight additional empty/padding/constructor cases began green and are characterization. Both transports preserve known binary content and SDK identity/equality. Binary limit thresholds, Storage blob/URL contracts, remaining scalars, marker collisions, qualified identity, overloads and event/capture propagation remain required.

Pyric, CLI and the embedded Studio/site were rebuilt before final browser verification. Earlier live-emulator and broader state/CLI evidence remains historical; no live backend was contacted or remote CI run claimed.
The additional S3 BridgeMount API seam remains pending; no tests at that interface have been authored.

Source identity covers changed files; a full transitive-input and completion verifier remains unfinished. Hosted authority/persistence, observation/Studio, reconnect/lifecycle, live surfaces and credential/release proofs remain required.

limits: Full goal, 0B, 2A/2D, U4/U6/U7 and implementation/release gates remain open. The listed cases do not establish complete runtime support.

Four S1 cycles establish served GeoPoint/vector exports, SDK class decoding, and explicit input encoding before SharedWorker cloning. All red assertions reached the SDK operation. GeoPoint writes are checked by rules requiring latlng; vectors are verified through SDK identity, components, and equality, without inventing a rules vector type test.

The existing GeoPoint and VectorValue implementations moved unchanged into browser-safe leaves before decoder changes. Separate review names validation decisions and preserves marker-first short-circuiting, coordinate validation order, vector component validation, and property-access timing. The decoder reuses existing vector JSON validation and retains rules wrappers for unary persistence callers.

Twelve additional cases began green and are characterization: GeoPoint zero/minimum/maximum/JSON coordinates and vector default-empty/JSON components over both transports. Full nested and non-finite values, marker collisions, qualified identity, overloads, and event/capture propagation remain required.

Pyric, CLI and the embedded Studio/site were rebuilt before final browser verification. Earlier live-emulator and broader state/CLI evidence remains historical; no live backend was contacted or remote CI run claimed.
The additional S3 BridgeMount API seam remains pending; no tests at that interface have been authored.

Source identity covers changed files; a full transitive-input and completion verifier remains unfinished. Hosted authority/persistence, observation/Studio, reconnect/lifecycle, live surfaces and credential/release proofs remain required.

limits: Full goal, 0B, 2A/2C/2D, U4/U6/U7 and implementation/release gates remain open. These scenarios do not establish complete runtime support.

Three S1/S2 cycles establish marker-shaped user maps alongside real SDK scalars, preserve an unversioned consumer map resembling the new escape marker, and reject an unsupported encoding before mutation without harming a second client.

The existing leaf codec owns the map escape and encoding declaration. Metadata is outside document fields and carried through write/query descriptors, snapshots and transaction read sets. The unary persistence decoder remains legacy; current remote reads honor reply declarations, but remote writers and durable formats still need explicit adoption/migration.

Eleven additional map scenarios began green and are characterization: SDK, rules, vector, recursive escape, unknown-marker and nested-array maps across hosted and SharedWorker. Complete operation/event/capture propagation, non-finite values, write-intent collisions, limits, qualified identity and overloads remain required.

The hosted legacy remote-channel attempt failed before the target assertion because the hosted peer does not yet advertise the old worker relay. That log is diagnostic only. The relevant compatibility red/green uses the established SharedWorker consumer relay.

Review names transaction canonicalization decisions, retains short-circuiting and repeated snapshot-data access, removes non-null assertions, and uses discriminant switches. Removing existing batch/transaction adapter assertions exposed a mismatch in the public modular declarations; the original assertions remain and the API/type correction is required work. Wrapper-clone canonicalization still needs complete collision/fidelity verification.

Pyric, CLI and the embedded Studio/site were rebuilt before final browser verification. No live backend was contacted or remote CI run claimed. New-client/old-receiver negotiation and refusal remain unproven; the versioned encoding field alone does not establish cross-version support.

The additional S3 BridgeMount API seam remains pending; no tests at that interface have been authored. Full transitive-input/schema completion verification, authority/persistence, observation/Studio, reconnect/lifecycle, live surfaces and credential/release proofs remain required.

limits: Full goal, 0B, 2A/2B/2C/2D, U4/U6/U7 and implementation/release gates remain open. These results are scoped evidence, not completion of the runtime contract.

Three S1 cycles establish batch merge:true, selected nested mergeFields, and invalid-argument with unchanged data for a missing mask field. The final six-case fixture covers both host transports, request.resource and sibling getAfter. Three additional SharedWorker cases are characterization; no red failure was fabricated.

The batch adapter retains merge intent and the shared atomic pipeline applies the existing merge engine before rules and storage consume the resulting document. The shared merge engine rejects absent mask fields using the shared FirebaseError type.

An existing Admin regression expected a missing mask field to be silently skipped. The installed Firebase 12.13.0 parseSetData implementation rejects it. The regression now checks invalid-argument and unchanged data through its public document handle. This strengthens the contract; it is not an exemption or a weakened assertion.

Transaction merge options, same-path operation composition, mutation of queued inputs, conflicting/invalid option combinations, complete field-mask and transform validation, client-side validation timing, event/capture/replay intent and public modular batch/transaction type alignment remain required.

Pyric, CLI and embedded Studio/site were rebuilt before final browser verification. All recorded final checks returned zero. No external Firebase backend or remote CI run is claimed; SDK-source inspection is not an upstream execution test.

Wire negotiation, complete codecs and remote/persistence adoption, authority/persistence, observation/Studio, reconnect/lifecycle, broad live execution and credential/release proofs remain open. The additional S3 BridgeMount interface is still pending; no test at it was authored.
Evidence binds the recorded candidate and artifacts. Complete transitive-input/schema verification and full U7 completion machinery remain unfinished.

Three S1 red/green cycles establish transaction merge:true, two merge:true writes to the same document, and selected nested mergeFields. The additional transport and refusal scenarios are green characterization.

Transaction.set forwards merge intent to the existing shared atomic pipeline. QueuedWrite reuses BatchOperationInput; same-path true-merge composition retains the prior intent. Field-mask validation and application reuse the shared merge engine. No new resource owner or protocol was introduced.

General same-path correctness remains unproven. The transaction reducer combines raw input before resolving transforms; masks, repeated transforms, updates, deletion, and queued-input lifetime need further public behavior proofs and an ordered write-intent solution. The simple two-merge proof is not general composition evidence.

Single-write transaction mask behavior now retains the selected data through request rules and sibling getAfter. Missing mask fields reject with invalid-argument without changing the document. limits: Full goal and all incomplete subsection/integration/release gates remain open. These results establish tested atomic sequences, not full wire fidelity, lifecycle, durability, live execution, or release readiness.

Ordered existence validation accepts create/set followed by update. Rules methods derive from original existence and final projected state; original storage intent is retained. Shared preparation rejects delete then update with invalid-argument, before any mutation, while accepting delete then set, recreation followed by update, and repeated deletion.

Three S1 red/green cycles cover sequential existence, creation-rule selection, and structured delete/update refusal. Six verified behaviours are exercised across both write APIs and both host transports. Already-supported deletion cases and matrix extensions are green characterization, not fabricated red evidence.

The LocalState mechanical extraction passed 69 regressions before and after. Named-condition/narrowing review preserved backing reads, projection getter timing, version updates, original type exports, and known-value assertions. The current 310-test engine/store/branch/persistence suite also preserves aborted transaction diagnostics.

Remaining atomic work includes queued-input lifetime, complete invalid-option/mask/transform validation, public adapter types, permission/precondition precedence, direct raw-store resolution failures, and full event/capture/replay intent. The legacy exported reducer retains its previous contract and no longer executes transactions.

The new main commit e207262fe74626cbe610c6367ec1b0536b887c46 was fast-forwarded after verifying disjoint paths and backing up 133 changed/untracked files. All were preserved byte-for-byte. Current builds and integrated checks follow that update; earlier cycle evidence remains explicitly historical.
The real Firebase SDK oracle used disposable local emulators. No production Firebase writes, release publishing, remote CI run, or complete credential/live-instrumentation proof is claimed.

Evidence binding is a scoped local audit. Complete transitive/schema verification and U7 completion machinery remain unfinished. The additional S3 BridgeMount interface remains pending; no test at that interface was written.

Five S1 red/green cycles preserve in-page batch/transaction field masks, in-page batch nested updates, and hosted/in-page queued Date values. The reviewed 24-scenario matrix covers both APIs across hosted, SharedWorker and in-page paths; additional cases began green as characterization.

The existing timestamp marker encodes native Dates before transport; in-page copying detaches Dates without evaluating transforms. Both paths preserve queue-time values and the public Timestamp return shape. Rules require the stored value to be a timestamp.

The actual Firebase SDK oracle confirms Date capture against disposable local emulators. It also shows that Invalid Date stores as epoch while a valid Date outside Firestore range fails synchronously with invalid-argument. This slice does not establish invalid or out-of-range input parity.

Remaining queued-input work includes other mutable SDK/native values, own-key/class fidelity, invalid inputs and pending single-write options. Complete transform/mask validation, public types and event/capture/replay intent remain required.

Authoritative persistence, admission, reconnect and resource accounting, bounded observations, full live execution, credentials and release requirements remain unfinished. SharedWorker remains the default.

Strict production, fixture and tool types pass; browser bundles remain in budget. No remote CI, publishing or production Firebase execution is claimed. Main revision e207262f remains the integration baseline.
Evidence binding is a scoped local audit; complete U7 transitive/schema/completion machinery remains unfinished. The additional S3 BridgeMount interface remains pending and was not tested.

Nine S1 red/green cycles cover upper/lower Date bounds, in-page queue-time refusal, nanosecond range/error precedence, hosted storage precision, in-page rules precision, query timestamp precision, and default query ordering. The reviewed 54-case matrix spans both write APIs and all three execution paths where applicable; additional cases began green as characterization.

Timestamp constructor guards preserve raw valid components. Date copying reuses the factory without resolving transforms. The shared write converter applies microsecond precision before rules and storage, and query capture normalizes trusted timestamp identities for comparison and execution. The wire codec retains original precision.

Four legacy ordering cases were retained with SDK-confirmed expected results under ADR-0009’s independent correctness-fix provision.

Strict production, fixture and tool types pass; all browser budgets pass. No remote CI, publishing, production Firebase execution or full compatibility certification is claimed. Main revision e207262f remains the integration baseline.
Evidence binding is a scoped local audit. Complete U7 transitive/schema/completion machinery remains unfinished. The additional S3 BridgeMount interface remains pending and was not tested.

oracleRuns.scope: Firebase 12.13.0 converted transaction snapshot behavior against disposable local emulators; lazy invocation, missing documents and retained converter identity

limits: The full hosted/live implementation and release gates remain open. These five S1 cycles cover converted transaction document reads and reference preservation, not complete sections 2A or 2B.

Public type fixtures prove the selected converted document-read path in the modular and worker exports. Full writeBatch/transaction declarations, foreign-reference ownership refusal, converter removal/reapplication, toFirestore for converted writes, query/listener converters and complete snapshot overloads remain required.

The SDK oracle establishes lazy conversion and missing-document behavior; current browser converter assertions prove the model and a subsequent converted read. Do not equate these assertions with the full oracle property set.

Snapshot containers use the shared type-preserving copier. Complete mutable scalar and own-key fidelity, other invalid inputs, complete value encoding/adoption, events/capture/replay and raw-store fault atomicity remain unproven.

Core lifecycle, durable authority, bounded observations, full live execution, credential management and release/packaging verification remain required. No production writes, remote CI, publishing or deployment is claimed.

Earlier failed build/selection attempts and the initial 30-of-31 review are diagnostics, not passing evidence. Final current checks below supersede their product-result claims without erasing the original failure transcripts.

limits: Full hosted/live implementation and release gates remain open. These six S1 cycles cover factory converter removal and basic converted set writes, not complete sections 2A or 2B.

Public fixtures prove selected model writes and converter removal/reapplication through both adapters without model index signatures or assertions. Full DbModel/generic constraints, overloads, converter option forwarding, synchronous exception timing and worker transaction chaining remain required.

Other reference producers, including addDoc and unconverted snapshot.ref methods, still need lifecycle coverage. Query/listener converter behavior, foreign-reference ownership, invalid-value refusal and update-with-converter behavior remain required.

The raw-data assertion in modular atomic conversion follows the existing unconverted document-record contract. This does not establish runtime validation for arbitrary invalid values or prove full generic adapter compatibility.

The modular batch preserves the existing per-commit sandbox auth override. Current legacy auth/identity regressions pass; no new production credential behavior or elevated execution policy is introduced.

Complete wire adoption/validation, durable authority, resource lifecycle, bounded observations, full live execution and credential management remain required. No production writes, publishing, deployment or remote CI execution is claimed.

An initial in-page batch build failed because OperationOptions is declared in its local type module rather than the public admin-firestore barrel. The corrected build passes; that compile failure is not behavior-red evidence.

limits: Full hosted/live implementation and release gates remain open. Four S1/S2 cycles cover unknown atomic methods, null write descriptors, non-array write lists and a non-array transaction read set. The 14-case real-transport matrix is partial 2C evidence.

The list assertion proves only the outer array. Individual transaction read entries, serialized read data, complete write option/value schemas, other path fields, malformed envelopes, session/version admission and size/depth limits remain required.

Unknown-method red evidence shows a partial commit through the healthy client. Malformed read-set red evidence shows both writes committed after an empty string was treated as zero reads. Null descriptor and non-array write-list reds show generic unknown errors rather than the required invalid-argument.

Current reports do not establish complete wire adoption, authoritative durability, host resource lifecycle, bounded observations, full live execution or credential isolation. No production writes, publishing, deployment or remote CI execution is claimed.

limits: Full implementation and release gates remain open. The two red/green cycles cover identity-protected Firestore listener restoration and prompt RTDB onDisconnect execution after physical socket loss.
The grant store has 60-second expiry and generation leases, but complete expiry, duplicate attachment, stale callback/cleanup, admission and retained-resource bounds are not proven by these cases.

RTDB .info/connected currently returns a fixed value. Connectivity notifications, new online generations, goOffline/goOnline and other service subscription recovery still need their gates. Draining disconnect work alone does not complete 3D.

Heartbeat detection, no-progress recovery bounds, new subscriptions during interruption, full tenant/lens restoration, pending boot/shutdown accounting, persistence and observation durability remain unfinished.

The CLI and Studio were rebuilt; unchanged Pyric source and artifact identities are explicitly reused. Earlier SDK/value/engine reports remain historical. A sandbox-denied bridge listening failure was preserved and the unchanged suite passed with local networking enabled.
No production writes, publishing, deployment or remote CI execution is claimed. Full wire, hosted persistence, observation, live execution, credentials and release gates remain open.

Review renames the app-controlled state to distinguish it from actual connectivity, and expands browser characterization across hosted and SharedWorker, per-client isolation and explicit offline state through socket recovery.

review.scope: The hosted CLI owns a non-blocking SQLite write reservation before configuration/state loading. Runtime-selected built-in SQLite replaces the incompatible native addon without any package or lockfile change. The reservation survives aliases and releases on process termination; BEGIN IMMEDIATE avoids the demonstrated simultaneous-start upgrade race. A separate helper extraction preserved all four prior scenarios before adding five review scenarios. Nine CLI cases pass under Node 22.18.0 and the minimum Node 22.15.0, with Bun 1.3.9 in both ownership directions. Twenty explicit race repetitions pass without retries. The copied standalone binary excludes Node and serves a normal SDK read from the MCP-written host store.

limits: These are partial 3B-MCP proofs, not full subsection, feature or release completion.
Only eight affected stdio scenarios were executed; all 391 scenarios were collected. The preceding 389-case browser, Studio, broad-regression and minimum-Node runs remain historical.
The current standalone cases verify packaged ownership, SDK and stdio discovery. They do not independently run the two HTTP fault scenarios inside the compiled proxy.
Complete unsent/refused/uncertain outcome classification, late replies, pending/settled bounds and shutdown accounting remain required.
Context headers are not authentication; complete admission, older-host refusal, authoritative all-service persistence, all writer entry points and durable acknowledgments remain required.
Complete service/control parity, atomic replacement, bounded observations and browser/hosted live execution remain required.
No full supported OS/runtime/package matrix, remote CI, production access, deployment or publishing is claimed.
